faq.q: How much does a photo booth cost for a wedding?
faq.a: WeddingWire puts the average wedding photo booth rental at $650, with most couples spending between $425 and $1,000, and packages starting around $551 for three hours. A rental usually includes an attendant and setup. A DIY booth costs about $68 in light and backdrop stand as of November 2026, or about $277 with a printer and 108 prints.

faq.q: Is a DIY photo booth worth it?
faq.a: Usually, if you have a free afternoon and a friend who will check on it during the reception. You save hundreds of dollars and control the look completely. What you give up is an attendant, fast printing and having someone else be responsible for it all. For a large wedding with a big printing queue, a rental is often less stressful.

faq.q: What do you need for a DIY wedding photo booth?
faq.a: A phone or iPad on a stand, a ring light at the lens, a backdrop stand with fabric or flowers, tape to mark where guests stand, and a sign explaining what to do. Add a compact photo printer if you want prints, and an app with a booth mode for countdowns and strips. Run everything on wall power.

faq.q: How long should the photo booth be open at a wedding?
faq.a: Booths rent by the hour, and WeddingWire lists starting packages around three hours. That fits most receptions: open it after dinner and the speeches, then keep it running through the dancing and the late-night stretch, when guests are most relaxed and groups form easily.

faq.q: How do guests get their photo booth pictures?
faq.a: Rented booths usually print strips on the spot and often share digital copies too. With a DIY or phone booth, you can print on a compact printer, AirDrop or text strips straight away, or add them to a shared camera roll so everyone sees them together at the reveal.
